Subject: MAP + next steps for MSA/DPA redlines (timeline & owners)

Hi Mike — thanks again for the time today. Attached is the draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we discussed. I pulled out the legal milestone as its own line so we can be explicit about who will own redlines, acceptable turnaround windows, and the target close date.

Quick summary of requests for your side:
- Please confirm whether Acme Legal will own initial redlines for MSA/DPA (we understand some customers prefer vendor-led redlines).
- If Acme Legal will own edits, can they commit to a 3 business-day turnaround on first-pass redlines? If not, what is the typical SLA?
- Any specific security/retention requirements you want called out in the DPA now so we can align legal and engineering early.

Attached: ACME_MAP_v1.docx (MAP draft), ACME_MSA_redlines_requested.pdf (redline template + questions)

Proposed internal owners from our side:
- Rishi Malhotra — primary legal reviewer and redline owner (1st pass)
- Priyom Das — commercial lead to coordinate pricing/terms items and escalation
- Marissa Cole — CS escalation contact for SLA and onboarding commitments

Target close on the MAP: 2026-05-14 (dependent on two rounds of redlines + DocuSign).

Next step: can you confirm ownership and turnaround by end of day Friday? Once we have that we will set the MAP milestones to reflect the agreed SLAs.

Thanks,
Olga

Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + next steps for MSA/DPA redlines (timeline & owners)

Thanks, Olga — good call earlier. A few quick answers:
- Acme Legal prefers to own initial redlines for MSA/DPA on larger contracts; they will take point here.
- Typical turnaround for first-pass redlines is 5 business days at our scale. We can try to compress to 3 days if needed but I can't promise until legal confirms.
- For the DPA: we need data residency language for EU customers and a standard 30-day log retention for audit logs.

I've looped in legal on this thread (legal@acme-analytics.com) — they'll confirm ownership and turnaround formally.

Also: can Redwood confirm whether SLAs in the MAP will be the operational SLA (platform uptime) or a commercial SLA that feeds into penalty terms? Our procurement is sensitive to penalty language.

Best,
Mike
VP, Platform Partnerships | Acme Analytics
mike.turner@acme-analytics.com

Thanks for the context, Olga. I confirm Redwood legal will be the primary owner for producing the counter-redlines and for tracking the MAP legal milestone. My proposed timeline:
- Day 0 (receipt of Acme first-pass redlines): Rishi acknowledges within 4 business hours and triages to engineering/commercial if there are technical/ops items
- Day 1-2: Internal review and prepare counter-redlines (3 business days total for a full counter-draft)
- Day 3-5: Buffer for coordination with engineering or additional commercial input; if we anticipate schedule slips we will raise an escalation and request a synchronous session with Acme within 2 business days

Escalation matrix:
- If two rounds of redlines are completed without convergence, Priyom and Marissa will schedule a call with Acme legal and their procurement lead.
- If Acme requests penalty-based SLA terms, I will not agree without VP Legal approval. Priyom please flag deals where SLAs include financial penalty language.

Action items I will do by EOD tomorrow:
1) Populate the MAP legal milestone with the above timeline and add Rishi (owner) + Priyom (commercial) as contacts
2) Attach our standard MSA redline baseline (redlines_redline_v2.docx) and call out the DPA residency/retention clauses to be reviewed by engineering

Marissa: pinging you for the customer success SLA acceptance criteria so I can include those in the MAP (uptime definitions, measurement windows, credits vs remediation).
